category: Verification & validation: Simulink Test, Requirements Toolbox, Coverage, Design Verifier & Check
description: Programmatic and block-level interfaces of the Simulink verification toolboxes: test harnesses, Test Manager files and reports, Test Sequence/Assessment blocks, requirement sets and traceability links, model coverage collection and reporting, formal test generation and property proving, clone detection and model slicing.

tools.name: sltest.testmanager.view
tools.description: Opens the Simulink Test Manager, the app for authoring test files, test suites and test cases (baseline, equivalence, simulation), running them and inspecting results. Use it after loading or creating test files from a script to inspect them interactively.
tools.example:
sltest.testmanager.load('controller_tests.mldatx');
sltest.testmanager.view;
tools.notes: Headless CI runs do not need the app: use sltest.testmanager.run and sltest.testmanager.report.

tools.name: sltest.testmanager.load
tools.description: Loads a Simulink Test file (.mldatx) into the Test Manager and returns an sltest.testmanager.TestFile object for programmatic inspection or execution.
tools.notes: Use sltest.testmanager.clear to unload test files and sltest.testmanager.clearResults to delete results.

tools.name: sltest.testmanager.TestFile
tools.description: Class representing a Test Manager test file. Constructing it creates a new .mldatx file with a default test suite; methods create and retrieve test suites, run all tests and save the file.
tools.usage:
tf = sltest.testmanager.TestFile(filePath)
ts = createTestSuite(tf, name)
saveToFile(tf)

parameters.name: run
parameters.description: Run every enabled test and return an sltest.testmanager.ResultSet.

tools.notes: Test case types for createTestCase: 'simulation', 'baseline' and 'equivalence'.

tools.name: sltest.testmanager.TestCase
tools.description: Class for a single Test Manager test case: which model or harness to simulate, parameter overrides, inputs, baseline or equivalence criteria, callbacks and iterations. Obtained from createTestCase on a test suite or getTestCases.
tools.usage:
tc = createTestCase(ts, type, name)
setProperty(tc, 'Model', mdl)
result = run(tc)

parameters.name: setProperty(tc, Name, Value)
parameters.description: Set Model, HarnessName, StopTime, OverrideStopTime, SimulationMode, etc.

parameters.name: addInput / addBaselineCriteria / captureBaselineCriteria
parameters.description: Attach external inputs and baseline data files.

tools.notes: Test cases can also run in multiple releases (setProperty 'Release').

tools.name: sltest.testmanager.report
tools.description: Generates a PDF, DOCX or ZIP (HTML) report from Test Manager results, optionally including coverage, simulation plots and only failed or passed tests. Standard final step of a CI test run.

parameters.name: resultObj
parameters.description: ResultSet or test result object(s) from run.

parameters.name: filePath
parameters.description: Output file; the extension selects the format.

tools.example:
rs = sltest.testmanager.run;
sltest.testmanager.report(rs, 'results.pdf', 'Title', 'Nightly', 'IncludeTestResults', 0, 'IncludeCoverageResult', true, 'LaunchReport', false);
tools.notes: For JUnit XML output in CI, use the MATLAB unit test runner with sltest.plugins.TestManagerResultsPlugin instead.

tools.name: sltest.testmanager.clearResults
tools.description: Clears all results from the Results and Artifacts pane of the Test Manager, freeing memory between test runs in long scripted sessions.
tools.example:
sltest.testmanager.clearResults;
rs = sltest.testmanager.run;
tools.notes: Does not unload test files; use sltest.testmanager.clear for that.

tools.name: sltest.testmanager.createTestForComponent
tools.description: Creates test cases and test harnesses for a model or model component in one step, optionally using logged or Design Verifier generated inputs. A quick way to scaffold regression tests for existing components.

parameters.name: TestFile
parameters.description: Test file to create or add to.

parameters.name: UseComponentInputs / TopModel
parameters.description: Record component inputs from a top-model simulation.

tools.example: tc = sltest.testmanager.createTestForComponent('Component', 'plant/Controller', 'TestFile', 'ctrl_tests.mldatx', 'TestType', 'baseline');
tools.notes: Check the documentation of your release for the exact name-value options.

tools.name: sltest.harness.create
tools.description: Creates a test harness for a model or component: an isolated model, stored with or beside the main model, that feeds the component from configurable sources and logs it to sinks. Harnesses keep test scaffolding out of the design model.

parameters.name: Source
parameters.description: Input source, e.g. 'Inport', 'Signal Editor', 'Test Sequence', 'From Workspace', 'Constant'.

parameters.name: SaveExternally
parameters.description: true stores the harness in its own file instead of inside the model.

tools.notes: The harness keeps a link to the component under test; changes sync back according to the synchronization mode.

tools.name: sltest.harness.open
tools.description: Opens a named test harness associated with a model or component in the Simulink Editor.

parameters.name: harnessOwner
parameters.description: Model or block that owns the harness.

tools.notes: Use sltest.harness.load to load a harness without opening a window, e.g. in headless runs.

tools.name: sltest.harness.find
tools.description: Lists the test harnesses of a model or component and returns a structure array of their properties (name, owner, source, sink, save location).

parameters.name: Name
parameters.description: Filter by harness name (supports regular expressions with 'RegExp','on').

parameters.name: SearchDepth
parameters.description: Limit how deep the search goes in the hierarchy.

tools.example:
h = sltest.harness.find('controller');
{h.name}
tools.notes: Pass the model name to search every component harness in it.

tools.name: sltest.harness.load
tools.description: Loads a test harness into memory without displaying it, suitable for scripted simulation and batch testing.
tools.example:
sltest.harness.load('controller/PID', 'PID_TS');
out = sim('PID_TS');
tools.notes: Only one harness per owner can be active at a time.

tools.name: Test Sequence
tools.description: Block that defines test inputs as a sequence of steps with actions and transition conditions, written in MATLAB action language with temporal operators (after, duration, et) and verify statements. It produces complex, reactive stimuli that respond to model outputs.
tools.usage: Simulink Test library: add_block('sltestlib/Test Sequence', [mdl '/TS'])  |  or harness Source = 'Test Sequence'

parameters.name: Steps
parameters.description: Hierarchical steps, each with an action (e.g. 'u = 5;') and transitions (e.g. 'after(2, sec)').

parameters.name: Symbols
parameters.description: Inputs, outputs, local data, parameters and constants of the block.

parameters.name: Scenarios
parameters.description: Optional alternative step sets selectable per test case.

tools.notes: Implemented on Stateflow technology; view executed steps with the Test Sequence step highlighting or Sequence Viewer.

tools.name: Test Assessment
tools.description: Block that evaluates model outputs against requirements during simulation using a step-based or when-decomposition table of verify and assert statements. Results appear in the Test Manager and Simulation Data Inspector as pass/fail signals.

parameters.name: Steps
parameters.description: Assessment steps with verify(...) statements and transitions.

tools.example:
% In the Test Assessment editor:
% step Monitor:  verify(abs(err) < 0.05, 'ctrl:tracking', 'Tracking error too large')
tools.notes: Test Assessment has no outputs; it only records verification results. Consider Requirements Table or temporal assessments in the Test Manager as alternatives.

tools.name: verify
tools.description: Assessment statement used in Test Sequence, Test Assessment and Stateflow blocks (and MATLAB Function blocks with Simulink Test) that records pass, fail or untested at each evaluation of a logical expression. Failed verify statements make the enclosing test case fail without stopping the simulation.

parameters.name: identifier
parameters.description: Colon-separated ID used to name the result in the Test Manager.

parameters.name: message
parameters.description: Failure message; may contain format operators followed by values.

tools.example: verify(speed <= limit, 'SpeedCtrl:limit', 'Speed %f exceeds limit', speed)
tools.notes: Use assert instead when a failure should stop the simulation.

tools.name: sltest.import.sldvData
tools.description: Creates Test Manager test cases and harnesses from Simulink Design Verifier results, turning generated test vectors or counterexamples into executable regression tests.

parameters.name: dataFile
parameters.description: Design Verifier data file (sldvData .mat) produced by sldvrun.

parameters.name: TestHarnessName / TestFileName
parameters.description: Names for the created harness and test file.

parameters.name: CreateHarness
parameters.description: Whether to create a new harness.

tools.example:
[status, files] = sldvrun('controller', sldvoptions);
sltest.import.sldvData(files.DataFile, 'TestFileName', 'sldv_tests.mldatx');
tools.notes: Combine with coverage collection to confirm the imported tests reach the expected coverage.

tools.name: slreq.new
tools.description: Creates a new requirement set (.slreqx) and returns an slreq.ReqSet object. Requirements are then added with add(rs, ...), organised hierarchically and saved with save(rs).

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Requirement set name or file path.

tools.notes: Requires Requirements Toolbox. Requirement sets can also be edited in the Requirements Editor (slreq.editor).

tools.name: slreq.load
tools.description: Loads a requirement set or link set file into memory and returns its object, so requirements and links can be queried and modified programmatically.
tools.notes: slreq.clear unloads all requirement and link sets.

tools.name: slreq.editor
tools.description: Opens the Requirements Editor, the app for authoring, importing, organising and reviewing requirements, viewing links, and inspecting implementation and verification status.
tools.example:
slreq.load('CruiseReqs.slreqx');
slreq.editor;
tools.notes: In a model, the Requirements Manager perspective (Apps > Requirements Manager) shows the same data beside the diagram.

tools.name: slreq.createLink
tools.description: Creates a traceability link from a source (model block, test case, code, requirement) to a destination (usually a requirement), for example an Implement or Verify link. Links are stored in a link set (.slmx) next to the source artifact.

parameters.name: src
parameters.description: Source item: block handle/path, Stateflow object, test case, requirement or slreq structure.

tools.notes: Link types include Implement, Verify, Relate, Refine, Derive and Confirm; they drive the implementation and verification status metrics.

tools.name: slreq.find
tools.description: Finds loaded Requirements Toolbox objects (requirements, references, requirement sets, links, link sets) of a given type that match property values.
tools.notes: Only objects in loaded sets are found; load sets first with slreq.load.

tools.name: slreq.import
tools.description: Imports requirements from external documents (Word, Excel, ReqIF, DOORS and others) into a requirement set, either as read-only referenced requirements that can be updated from the source or as editable requirements.

parameters.name: AsReference
parameters.description: true (default) keeps a link to the source for later updates.

tools.example:
[n, f, rs] = slreq.import('SystemSpec.docx', 'ReqSet', 'SysSpec', 'RichText', true);
fprintf('%d requirements imported\n', n);
tools.notes: Excel import typically needs column mapping options; ReqIF preserves attributes from other tools.

tools.name: slreq.generateReport
tools.description: Generates a report (Word, PDF or HTML) for loaded requirement sets including requirements, links, implementation and verification status.

parameters.name: reqSet
parameters.description: slreq.ReqSet object or array; 'all' reports all loaded sets.

parameters.name: opts
parameters.description: Options structure from slreq.getReportOptions (reportPath, openReport, includes...).

tools.notes: Report generation uses MATLAB Report Generator technology; generating Word/PDF on Windows may require Microsoft Word.

tools.name: cvtest
tools.description: Creates a Simulink Coverage test specification object for a model or subsystem, holding which coverage metrics to collect and other settings. Pass it to cvsim to simulate and collect coverage.
tools.usage:
testObj = cvtest(root)
testObj = cvtest(root, label, setupCmd)

parameters.name: settings.decision / settings.condition / settings.mcdc
parameters.description: Enable decision, condition and MC/DC coverage (1/0).

parameters.name: settings.sigrange / settings.tableExec / settings.designverifier
parameters.description: Signal range, lookup table and Design Verifier block coverage.

parameters.name: label / setupCmd
parameters.description: Label for reports and a command run before simulation.

tools.notes: Alternatively enable coverage through model parameters (CovEnable, CovMetricStructuralLevel) and read out.covdata after sim.

tools.name: cvhtml
tools.description: Produces an HTML model coverage report from one or more cvdata objects, with per-block decision, condition, MC/DC and other metric details and links back to the model.
tools.usage:
cvhtml(fileName, cvdo)
cvhtml(fileName, cvdo1, cvdo2, ..., options)

parameters.name: cvdo
parameters.description: cvdata or cv.cvdatagroup objects; several are reported side by side.

parameters.name: options
parameters.description: Option string such as '-sRT=0' to not open the report.

tools.example:
cov1 = cvsim(t1); cov2 = cvsim(t2);
cvhtml('combined', cov1 + cov2, '-sRT=0');
tools.notes: Adding cvdata objects (cov1 + cov2) cumulates coverage across tests.

tools.name: cvsave
tools.description: Saves coverage test settings and results (cvtest and cvdata objects) to a .cvt file so coverage can be reloaded, cumulated or reported later.

parameters.name: cvdo
parameters.description: cvdata objects to save (or a model name to save all its results).

tools.example:
cov = cvsim(cvtest('controller'));
cvsave('nightly.cvt', cov);
tools.notes: Load with cvload; the model must be available when results are loaded.

tools.name: cvload
tools.description: Loads coverage tests and results from a .cvt file and returns cell arrays of cvtest and cvdata objects for reporting or aggregation.

parameters.name: restoreTotal
parameters.description: 1 restores cumulative results into the model's coverage data.

tools.example:
[~, data] = cvload('nightly.cvt');
cvhtml('nightly_report', data{1});
tools.notes: Loading coverage from an older model version may fail if the model structure changed.

tools.name: cvdata
tools.description: Object holding model coverage results for one test (or a cumulated set). Pass it to cvhtml for reports or to decisioninfo, conditioninfo, mcdcinfo and similar functions to extract numbers; cvdata objects support +, - and * to combine results.
tools.usage:
cov = cvsim(testObj)
cov = out.covdata   % when coverage is enabled via model parameters

parameters.name: test
parameters.description: The cvtest object used to collect the data.

tools.notes: Use cv.cvdatagroup when coverage spans several models in a reference hierarchy.

tools.name: decisioninfo
tools.description: Returns decision coverage for a model object from a cvdata object as [covered total] outcome counts, plus optional per-decision details. Use it to assert coverage thresholds in automated tests.
tools.usage:
coverage = decisioninfo(cvdo, modelObject)
[coverage, description] = decisioninfo(cvdo, modelObject)

parameters.name: modelObject
parameters.description: Model, subsystem, block path/handle, SID or Stateflow object.

tools.notes: Related: conditioninfo, mcdcinfo, executioninfo, sigrangeinfo, tableinfo.

tools.name: mcdcinfo
tools.description: Returns modified condition/decision coverage (MC/DC) for a model object from a cvdata object as [covered total] condition counts, with optional details of which conditions lack an independence pair.
tools.usage:
coverage = mcdcinfo(cvdo, modelObject)
[coverage, description] = mcdcinfo(cvdo, modelObject)
tools.example:
[c, d] = mcdcinfo(cov, 'controller/Logic');
fprintf('MC/DC %d of %d\n', c(1), c(2));
tools.notes: MC/DC is required for DO-178C Level A and ISO 26262 ASIL D structural coverage.

tools.name: CovEnable (model parameter)
tools.description: Model configuration parameter that turns on model coverage collection during normal simulation, so sim returns coverage data (out.covdata) without using cvtest/cvsim. Companion parameters select the metrics and reporting.

parameters.name: CovSaveSingleToWorkspaceVar / CovSaveName
parameters.description: 'on' stores the cvdata in the SimulationOutput under the name given by CovSaveName.

tools.notes: Found under Configuration Parameters > Coverage. Coverage adds instrumentation overhead; disable it for performance runs.

tools.name: sldvoptions
tools.description: Creates a Simulink Design Verifier options object that selects the analysis mode (test generation, design error detection, property proving), time limits, coverage objectives and which result artifacts are saved. Pass it to sldvrun or sldvcompat.
tools.notes: sldvoptions(model) returns the options stored in the model's configuration set.

tools.name: sldvcompat
tools.description: Checks whether a model or atomic subsystem is compatible with Simulink Design Verifier analysis, reporting unsupported blocks or features before a long analysis is started. Returns 1 when compatible.
tools.notes: Partial incompatibilities can often be handled by automatic stubbing, which the compatibility log describes.

tools.name: sldvruntest
tools.description: Simulates a model with the test cases generated by Design Verifier (from the sldvData file), optionally collecting model coverage, to confirm the generated tests reach their objectives.

parameters.name: runOpts
parameters.description: Options from sldvruntestopts (test indices, output format).

tools.notes: Use sltest.import.sldvData to turn the same data into Test Manager tests.

tools.name: Proof Objective
tools.description: Design Verifier block that states an invariant a signal must satisfy, expressed as allowed values or intervals. In property-proving mode the tool either proves the property or produces a counterexample.
tools.usage: Simulink Design Verifier library (sldvlib) > Objectives and Constraints > Proof Objective
tools.notes: Ignored during normal simulation and code generation. Place proofs inside a Verification Subsystem to keep them out of the design.

tools.name: Proof Assumption
tools.description: Design Verifier block that constrains signal values during property proving, e.g. limiting an input to its physical range so the prover does not consider impossible values.
tools.usage: Simulink Design Verifier library (sldvlib) > Objectives and Constraints > Proof Assumption

parameters.name: Values
parameters.description: Allowed values or intervals for the signal.

tools.example: % on input 'speed': Values = {Sldv.Interval(0, 250)}
tools.notes: Over-constraining with assumptions can hide real counterexamples; review them like requirements.

tools.name: Test Objective
tools.description: Design Verifier block that defines custom test-generation goals: values or ranges a signal must reach for at least one time step in the generated tests, in addition to structural coverage objectives.
tools.usage: Simulink Design Verifier library (sldvlib) > Objectives and Constraints > Test Objective

parameters.name: Values
parameters.description: Target values or intervals, e.g. '{1, 2, Sldv.Interval(90, 100)}'.

tools.example: % Values: {Sldv.Interval(95, 100)}  -> generate a test that drives temperature above 95
tools.notes: Used only in test-generation mode; ignored in simulation and code generation.

tools.name: Test Condition
tools.description: Design Verifier block that constrains signal values in generated test cases, e.g. keeping an input within a valid range. It can be switched to behave as a Proof Assumption.
tools.usage: Simulink Design Verifier library (sldvlib) > Objectives and Constraints > Test Condition

parameters.name: Values
parameters.description: Allowed values or intervals for the signal in generated tests.

tools.example: % on input 'gear': Values = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5}
tools.notes: Test conditions apply only to test generation; use Proof Assumption for proofs.

tools.name: Verification Subsystem
tools.description: Preconfigured subsystem for holding proof objectives, test objectives, assumptions and requirement logic that observe the design without affecting its simulation results or generated code.
tools.usage: Simulink Design Verifier library (sldvlib) > Verification Subsystem
tools.example:
% place Verification Subsystem next to the design, route observed signals in,
% and add Proof Objective / Test Objective blocks inside
tools.notes: Contents are excluded from code generation, so verification logic can live in the production model.

tools.name: Simulink.CloneDetection.findClones
tools.description: Simulink Check function that finds subsystem clones (exact or similar) in a model or across a library, returning a Simulink.CloneDetection.Results object that can be passed to Simulink.CloneDetection.replaceClones to refactor them into library links or subsystem references.

parameters.name: settings
parameters.description: Simulink.CloneDetection.Settings: ignore signal names/block properties, parameter difference threshold, libraries to match, excluded model references.

tools.notes: Interactive equivalent: Apps > Clone Detector. Back up or use source control before replacing clones.

tools.name: slslicer
tools.description: Creates a Model Slicer API object (SLSlicerAPI.SLSlicer) for a model to highlight the upstream or downstream dependencies of chosen starting points, restrict analysis to a simulation time window, and extract a simplified sliced model for debugging.
tools.usage:
obj = slslicer(model)
obj = slslicer(model, opts)   % opts from slsliceroptions

parameters.name: addStartingPoint / addExclusionPoint
parameters.description: Blocks, signals, bus elements or SIDs that seed or bound the slice.

parameters.name: activate / terminate
parameters.description: Start and end a slicing session.

parameters.name: highlight / slice
parameters.description: Highlight the slice or create a standalone sliced model.

tools.notes: Part of Simulink Check. Activating Model Slicer compiles the model and locks it for editing until terminated.
